humanTitle: People must install an app to see a ticket they bought
whoItAffects: Android users in the United States, across two app versions.

build.proposition: A ticket that exists outside the app that sold it.
specifics: Issue to the device wallet at purchase, not at the gate
Keep a printable fallback the venue can still scan
Draw the barcode from data already held on the device
build.limitation: A ticket that travels is also a ticket that resells, and controlling resale is why the app holds it.

start.proposition: Issuing that puts the ticket in the holder’s hands at the moment of sale.
specifics: Standard wallet passes, offline by default, no install required
Aimed at venues whose entry queue is the thing that fails
start.limitation: Venues buy ticketing from whoever runs the sale, so the person queuing is never the buyer being sold to.

study.proposition: What does a gate do when the barcode will not load?
specifics: Record entry failures at the door rather than inside the app
Compare venues that keep a box office fallback with those that do not
study.limitation: Entry data belongs to venues, and a failed entry is precisely what nobody wants recorded.

write.proposition: The ticket you paid for lives somewhere you cannot reach.
specifics: Follow one entry from the purchase page to the gate
Quote the reviewer told a digital wallet was an option
write.limitation: Ticketing anger is heavily covered; the barcode that never renders is the part that is not.
